title: Ajay Mehta v. Honda Motors
text: The complainant, Ajay Mehta, purchased a new car from the opposite party which developed serious manufacturing defects within three months of purchase. Despite six visits to the authorised service centre, the defects could not be rectified. The complainant sought replacement of the vehicle or refund before NCDRC. The opposite party denied manufacturing defect and attributed issues to misuse. The NCDRC appointed an independent technical expert whose report confirmed inherent manufacturing defects in the engine and gearbox. Supply of a defective product and failure to rectify it amounts to deficiency in service. The NCDRC directs the opposite party to replace the vehicle with a new one of the same model or refund the purchase price of Rs 12,00,000 with 9% interest. Compensation of Rs 1,00,000 for harassment is also awarded to the complainant.
